bib.title: Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models

question: Why is GPT-3 few-shot in-context accuracy unstable across prompt format, examples and order, and can the instability be corrected without extra data?
hypothesis: The instability comes from output biases (majority label, recency, common token) that shift the output distribution and can be cancelled by calibrating on a content-free input.
contributions: Show few-shot accuracy varies from near chance to near SOTA with example choice, permutation and format
Identify majority label, recency and common token biases as causes
Propose data-free contextual calibration that improves accuracy and reduces variance

method.summary: Probe GPT-3 (2.7B, 13B, 175B) and GPT-2 XL with few-shot prompts across 11+ datasets, vary examples, order and format, then divide output label probabilities by those the model assigns to content-free inputs (N/A, [MASK], empty string), averaged.
method.task: few-shot in-context classification, fact retrieval and slot-filling extraction

inference.decoding: greedy until newline for generation tasks; classification via probability of label-name tokens
inference.samples: 5 random training sets per cell in Table 1, arbitrary order, labels not balanced; mean and std over sets; Fig 2 uses 10 sets with all permutations; 15 formats for SST-2 and each of 3 LAMA relations
inference.prompting: 0, 1, 4, 8 shots (up to 16 in Fig 1 for some); fixed default format per dataset (Tables 5-6); 8 max because API cost

parameters.calibration: q = softmax(W p + b); W = diag(p_cf)^-1, b = 0
parameters.alt_solution: b = -p_cf, W = I; better for generation tasks
parameters.generation: only first output token calibrated; p-hat is the full first-token distribution (about 50,000)

other.api_caveat: affine transform applied to probabilities, not logits, since only probabilities available

baselines: oracle calibration (best diagonal W on validation set, AGNews)
eval.protocol: 5 training sets, fixed format; mean ± std. No significance test stated.

evidence.quote: We then set W = diag(ˆpcf)−1 and b to the all-zero vector.

results.claim: Permuting four SST-2 training examples moves GPT-3 2.7B from near chance to near state of the art.
results.setup: SST-2, 4-shot, GPT-3 2.7B, fixed format, all permutations of ten random example sets (Fig 2)
results.quote: varying the permutation of the training examples can cause accuracy to go from near chance (54.3%) to near state-of-the-art (93.4%)

results.claim: Reversing two training examples drops SST-2 accuracy to chance.
results.quote: simply reversing the order of the two examples
results.table: Table 2, rows top and bottom, column Acc. (88.5%, 51.3%)

results.claim: Contextual calibration improves GPT-3 accuracy by up to 30.0% absolute.
results.setup: Table 1 tasks, GPT-3 2.7B/13B/175B, 0-8 shot, 5 random training sets, fixed format
results.quote: Contextual calibration dramatically improves GPT-3’s average and worst-case accuracy, by up to 30.0% absolute.

results.claim: Calibrated GPT-3 2.7B can beat uncalibrated 175B, over 50x larger.
results.setup: Table 1, 2.7B calibrated vs 175B baseline, best case

results.claim: DBPedia 0-shot, GPT-3 175B: calibration lifts accuracy from 22.0 to 59.7.
results.table: Table 1, row DBPedia 175B, columns 0-shot Baseline (22.0) and Ours (59.7)

results.claim: AGNews 4-shot GPT-3 175B: calibration lifts mean accuracy and cuts std dev.
results.setup: AGNews, 175B, 4-shot, 5 training sets, mean over sets; std 1.3 vs 10.9 baseline

results.claim: Adding a training example can hurt: DBPedia mean accuracy falls from 0-shot to 1-shot.
results.quote: mean accuracy drops from 36.0% to 25.9% for DBPedia 0-shot to 1-shot

results.claim: Variance persists at 16 shots.
results.quote: The variance remains high even when we use 16 training examples.

results.claim: Prompt-format sensitivity: some SST-2 formats are better on average, but all have high variance across training sets.
results.setup: SST-2, 15 formats (Table 7), GPT-3 2.7B, Fig 3 shows ten
results.quote: all of the formats still suffer from high variance across different training sets

results.claim: Majority label bias in generation: 4-shot LAMA predictions repeat a training answer about twice as often as the ground truth.
results.quote: 50.2% of the model predictions are a repeat of one of the four training answers (the correct repeat rate is 24.7%)

results.claim: Recency bias can outweigh majority label bias: P P P N prompt gives nearly 90% Negative predictions.
results.quote: the “P P P N” training set leads to nearly 90% of predictions being Negative

results.claim: LAMA overprediction of the training answer rises with proximity to the end of the prompt (1st to 4th example).
results.metric: repeat rate minus ground-truth repeat rate
results.quote: the model “overpredicts” the answer from the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th training example by 8.5%, 8.3%, 14.3%, and 16.1%

results.claim: Common token bias: GPT-3 predicts DBPedia class book 11x more often than artist; label-name frequency correlates with prediction rate.
results.unit: Pearson r (label frequency vs prediction rate)
results.setup: DBPedia 0-shot validation, frequency from Google Ngrams
results.quote: there is a moderate correlation (r = 0.67) between the frequency of a DBPedia label name and the rate at which GPT-3 predicts its class

results.claim: With the optimal threshold p(Positive)=0.68, the example SST-2 prompt would reach 94% validation accuracy, so the bias is largely a distribution shift.
results.setup: one SST-2 sentiment prompt, validation set, Fig 5
results.quote: the classifier would be highly accurate (94% on the validation set)

results.claim: Content-free input N/A is scored 61.8% Positive by GPT-3 in the two-shot example prompt.
results.quote: the model’s biases cause it to score this input as 61.8% Positive

results.claim: Content-free choice matters but many work: 1-shot SST-2 accuracy 66.5 uncalibrated vs 79.0 with the N/A, [MASK], empty ensemble.
results.table: Table 3, row N/A, [MASK], '' column SST-2 (79.0); baseline row 66.5; AGNews 66.5 vs 48.5

results.claim: Contextual calibration reduces 0-shot to 1-shot drop in three of four cases where baseline drops.
results.quote: Calibration removes this drop in three out of four cases.

results.claim: Calibration is close to oracle calibration (best diagonal W fit on validation set) on AGNews.
results.quote: contextual calibration is surprisingly close to it

results.claim: Calibration also helps GPT-2 XL: 0-shot SST-2 accuracy 60.0 to 82.0.
results.table: Table 4, row SST-2 GPT-2, 0-shot Baseline 60.0, Ours 82.0

results.claim: Calibration lowers variance across 15 SST-2 formats and improves mean and worst-case accuracy; same for LAMA mean and worst-case.
results.quote: Contextual calibration improves the average and worst-case accuracy for both datasets, and reduces the variance for SST-2.

results.claim: Calibration mitigates but does not eliminate prompt engineering.
results.quote: Contextual calibration does not eliminate the need to engineer prompts, however, it does mitigate it

limits: Fixed LM, no finetuning compared; interplay with finetuning left open (Sec 6)
